We have included CA DSA Endorsements stand, where applicable. There are several races where we have not made a recommendation. articles.author: David A. Love
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. The future of the nation is in the South, the former Confederacy and ground zero of America’s civil rights struggles. We need only look to a place like Mississippi to understand the mess that is this settler colonial project called America, with its unaddressed and seemingly intractable internal contradictions. Mississippi has shown us the promise of Black power snuffed out by white supremacy, unjust laws and the Klan. Today, Mississippi is an example of how Black people are once again so close to cracking the code and freeing ourselves and the nation in the process. articles.author: Chuck Yates
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Several weeks ago, our college football team upset a higher-ranked opponent to remain undefeated. There was a lot of fist bumping among the fans as we all went home feeling vindicated for our faith in the team and the coaches. Before the game, as always, there was the National Anthem. articles.title: Medieval Egypt Was No Stranger to Class War
articles.author: Nicholas Liu
articles.content_excerpt: On Roda Island in the Nile stands a stone column nineteen cubits (thirty-four feet) tall and nearly 1,200 years old. It is called the Nilometer . Before the construction of the Aswan Dam, an official would measure how high the river rose and from that reading determine the fate of the country’s annual harvest. By the eleventh century and continuing until the Ottoman Turkish conquest of 1517, the rulers of Egypt had made a tradition of exorbitant pageantry whenever the waterline reached sixteen cubits: the harvest would be reaped, the cosmic and communal order confirmed, the people fed and placated, and the land tax collected. articles.content_excerpt: Mike Wallace once handed me a matchbook, the kind of paper trinket that served like ticker-tape as a currency of the twentieth-century city: given out at corner stores and newsstands, boxing matches and cafeterias, free-flowing from cigarette and candy booths on subway platforms. articles.author: Justin Mayhugh
articles.content_excerpt: With less than two weeks until Election Day, the UAW is leading its most ambitious political operation in decades in some of the country’s most critical and high-profile races. articles.title: Profits Are Soaring. Workers’ Share of Income Is Sinking.
articles.author: Conor Lynch
articles.content_excerpt: Outside periods of recession, the public mood has rarely been as downbeat about the economy as it is today, with consumer confidence at a historic low and polls recording a deep pessimism about where things are headed. Against this backdrop, political and business leaders are touting an economic “golden age,” pointing to solid growth , stable unemployment, record profits , and a stock market that seems to only go up. The vibes on Main Street are gloomy, but on Wall Street they are nearly euphoric. One way to understand this growing disconnect between everyday people and elites is to examine how today’s celebrated gains are distributed across the economy compared with earlier periods. articles.author: Rochester Red Star: News from Rochester DSA
articles.content_excerpt: by Greg B. Many people in Rochester DSA have asked whether the chapter should release a voter guide for the 2026 elections, and we’ve debated it in our Electoral Working Group. Unlike other organizations, DSA’s endorsements are highly selective and usually go to candidates who are members, agree to join, and help grow DSA; members often view a voter guide as a way to guide non-member supporters on our perspective on an election. Others think it’s a waste of time and misleading since people often confuse our “recommendation” for an actual endorsement. After examining the 2026 general election ballot, I’ve decided to recommend the chapter not make a voter guide. articles.title: Isabella Weber on How to Defeat the Far Right
articles.author: Isabella Weber
articles.content_excerpt: The economist Isabella Weber is best known for her work on what is often called “seller’s inflation,” the ability of firms with market power to hike prices and boost profits during an emergency. During and after the Covid-19 pandemic, Weber was one of the loudest voices criticizing those who treated inflation purely as a product of too much demand, earning the censure of establishment economists in the process. Six years on, her arguments have been largely vindicated. It is clear that while constraints to supply did cause some prices to spike, the resulting cost shocks coordinated corporate pricing that spread inflation across the whole economy. articles.title: The Green Party Will Regain Momentum if It Keeps Its Nerve
articles.author: Daniel Finn
articles.content_excerpt: On October 8, the Green Party fell short in a parliamentary by-election for the London constituency of Holborn and St Pancras that had been triggered by the resignation of Keir Starmer. The by-election was always going to be a long shot for the Green leader Zack Polanski, who stood as the party’s candidate. The result, which saw Labour retain the seat, was broadly what you would have expected from the current state of national opinion polls. That hasn’t stopped much of the British media from proclaiming the outcome to have been a game-changing disaster for the Greens and Polanski in particular.
